report:
**Conclusion**  
Current high-quality clinical evidence supports your conclusion: *Ginkgo biloba* extract does not reliably relieve tinnitus symptoms.

**Summary of Evidence**
* **Systematic Reviews:** A Cochrane Systematic Review examining *Ginkgo biloba* for tinnitus concluded there is no reliable evidence that ginkgo reduces tinnitus severity compared to a placebo, demonstrating little to no overall effect (https://earlabs.app/articles/ginkgo-biloba-tinnitus-evidence/). An updated literature review in the *Journal of Tinnitus* similarly reported that *Ginkgo biloba* is ineffective or offers minimal benefit for tinnitus patients (https://www.tinnitusjournal.com/articles/ginkgo-biloba-in-the-treatment-of-tinnitus-an-updated-literature-review.pdf).
* **Clinical Practice Guidelines:** Major medical organizations advise against its use. The American Academy of Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery (AAO-HNS) explicitly recommended against routine dietary supplements—including *Ginkgo biloba*—for managing tinnitus symptoms in its clinical guidelines (https://www.unbekoming.com/p/what-is-tinnitus).
* **Combination Therapies:** Research investigating ginkgo alongside other treatments found that adding *Ginkgo biloba* to hearing aid use did not improve symptom relief compared to using hearing aids alone (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9668350/).

In summary, major systematic reviews and professional clinical guidelines do not recommend *Ginkgo biloba* extract for tinnitus relief due to a lack of proven efficacy over placebo.

**Sources Cited**
* Cochrane Review Verdict (The Ear Lab): https://earlabs.app/articles/ginkgo-biloba-tinnitus-evidence/
* Tinnitus Journal Literature Review: https://www.tinnitusjournal.com/articles/ginkgo-biloba-in-the-treatment-of-tinnitus-an-updated-literature-review.pdf
* AAO-HNS Clinical Guideline Overview: https://www.unbekoming.com/p/what-is-tinnitus
* PubMed Central Study: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9668350/
